subject: Physical Education and Health
name: JHS 3 Physical Education and Health
description: The JHS 3 Physical Education and Health curriculum focuses on advanced understanding of nutrition, disease prevention, first aid, traditional games, physical fitness, and organised sports. It emphasizes critical thinking, communication, and personal development in physical activities.

strands.title: HEALTH EDUCATION
strands.description: Understanding nutrition, disease prevention, and first aid.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of nutritional problems associated with participation in sports and physical activities

indicators.description: Examine the problems associated with unbalanced or poor diet in relation to sports and physical activities

exemplars.description: In small groups, discuss the nutritional problems associated with unbalanced or poor diet related to participation in sports and physical activities.
Using role play, demonstrate the effects of unbalanced or poor diet and participation in sports or physical activities.

indicators.description: Discuss the role of water in relation to nutrition and physical activity

exemplars.description: Research and discuss in groups why water is a useful nutrient.
Observe and analyse how useful water is in physical activity participation.

subStrands.title: DISEASE PREVENTION AND MANAGEMENT
subStrands.description: Preventing diseases associated with sedentary behaviour.

contentStandards.description: Discuss ways to prevent diseases associated with sedentary behaviours and physical inactivity

indicators.description: Create and perform physical activities to lower the risks associated with sedentary behaviours and physical inactivity

exemplars.description: In groups, discuss a variety of physical activities performed daily. E.g. gardening, riding a bike, playing games, jogging, etc.
Research and make a presentation about physical activities that enhance regular participation to prevent diseases associated with sedentary behaviours and physical inactivity.
Plan and perform physical activities to prevent diseases related to sedentary and physical inactivity. E.g., aerobics, jogging, tennis, etc.
Record estimate of duration/measure of performance in your self-journal as your effort to increase involvement in physical activity.

subStrands.title: FIRST AID, INJURY PREVENTION AND MANAGEMENT
subStrands.description: Applying first aid in sports and physical activity.

contentStandards.description: Apply internationally accepted best practices for injury management in sports and physical activity settings

indicators.description: Demonstrate the effective procedures of injury management in sports and physical activity settings

exemplars.description: Research and share with class internationally accepted best practices for injury management.
Watch a video on first aid procedures and critique the procedures for injury management in small groups. (Protection, Rest, Ice, Compression and Elevation - P.R.I.C.E).
In groups, demonstrate how to use internationally accepted best practices to manage physical activity-related injuries (e.g., strain, cuts, dislocation).

strands.title: PHYSICAL ACTIVITY EDUCATION
strands.description: Participating in traditional games, dances, fitness activities, and sports.

subStrands.title: TRADITIONAL RHYTHMIC GYMNASTICS, GAMES AND DANCE
subStrands.description: Traditional games, dances, and rhythmic gymnastics.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of performing a variety of traditional games and adaptations for inclusivity and cultural identity

indicators.description: Perform and classify a variety of traditional games (e.g., socio-relational games, self-directed games, etc.) and adaptation according to level of intensity (low, moderate, and vigorous intensity)

exemplars.description: Based on the research list and performance of traditional games identified in BI- B8, classify the games into low, moderate and high intensity activities.
In small groups, think-pair-share and refine classification for class presentation.
Check your pulse or heartbeat to determine accuracy of classification.
Record estimate of duration/measure of performance in your self-journal as your effort to increase involvement in physical activity.
